ResearcherNotesProject: GENUINE NEW DISCOVERY (not a dormant-revival case -- Melilla has no existing GEM LNG terminal record). Endesa Generacion S.A.U. and Enagas (via its Enagas Emprende subsidiary) jointly proposed a 5,000 m3 LNG storage + regasification plant at Muelle Nordeste III, Port of Melilla in June 2021, to feed Endesa's Melilla thermal power plant (converting from diesel/fuel-oil to gas) and provide bunkering to ships/ferries. Concrete steps taken: (1) Endesa requested a ~10,300 m2 administrative port concession from the Port Authority of Melilla (2024), triggering a formal competition-of-projects process; (2) the project was submitted to Spain's PERTE industrial-modernization fund. Sponsor + location + concrete regulatory step all clear the threshold (methodology SS3). SCOPE GATE: this is a marine LNG import (ship discharge -> onshore regas -> pipeline to power plant), not a domestic-only/virtual-pipeline case, so it clears the scope gate distinctly from the Los Barrios/Algeciras bunkering-only precedent (see qa note). CURRENT STATUS (as of 2026-07-29): the project is reported PARALYZED/stalled since February 2025 over a funding dispute between Endesa and the central government (who bears the diesel-to-gas conversion cost); PERTE explicitly excludes regulated territorial-monopoly utilities like Endesa, so the company is seeking an alternative route; next PERTE call is February 2026, with a December 2025 deadline flagged in coverage, after which Melilla would have to wait for the next EU funding cycle (~2028) if unresolved. Staged as Status=proposed (not shelved) because the funding dispute itself is recent/ongoing reporting (2025-2026), not a multi-year silence -- this is an active-but-stalled regulatory/financing fight, distinguishable from the Discovery SOP's 'no apparent activity since' shelved case. Capacity intentionally left blank: 5,000 m3 is a STORAGE volume (confirmed on 3 independent sources), not an annual throughput/mtpa figure; no send-out rate was found. dedup_index.py match: discovery_new (no similar existing GEM terminal in Spain/Melilla).
